newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Globe sets 1997 capex at 7.6 bln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Globe sets 1997 capex at 7.6 bln pesos.

text.p: Globe Telecom GMCR Inc, a joint venture of Ayala Corp and Singapore Telecom, said on Monday its capital expenditure for 1997 will amount to 7.6 billion pesos.

In a press statement, the cellular mobile phone company and international gateway facility (IGF) operator said the amount will be used primarily for nationwide build-up of its cellular mobile network and fixed telephone infrastructure.

Globe announced its 1997 capex after the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) approved a 1.6 billion peso stock rights offer involving 133.33 million shares at a rate of 12 pesos a share to stockholders as of February 6, 1997.
The company said proceeds of the offer will be used to finance in part its expansion programme.
Globe has estimated a net loss of 750 million pesos for 1996 owing to hefty expenditures on its expansion projects and the start-up of its telecom operations.
For 1997, the company expects a lower net loss of 321.2 million pesos as its cellular operations have started to register earnings in the last quarter of 1996 and is seen to continue this year.
Globe is required to install 700,000 landlines in exchange for its cellular and IGF permit.
